feedback: Ada: The line was printed yesterday, and the recording shows the cup breaking within the stated minute. That match is documented; how the advance information arrived is still a question.
Ada: We set a stop condition before observing. A prediction matching this break has not earned the right to command our hands; it remains evidence to investigate.

Ada: Sera said we could put the cup on the floor and observe that intervention. We chose a guarded observation, with a stop condition for danger. That procedure creates no rule that a cup cannot be moved.

requiredPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredPassages.text: You clear the table edge, move the chair out of the likely fall area, and find a shallow conservation box for any fragments. Tomas positions the camera so the clock and cup can be seen together without anyone holding it. You mark the tripod's place with a small piece of removable tape.

requiredPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredPassages.text: You notice the cup's repair more clearly now. The adhesive line follows an old break around the handle's upper attachment. A slight discoloration suggests age or a previous unsuitable material. You do not poke it. The test is about the documented claim, not your ability to force the predicted outcome.

requiredPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredPassages.text: On a separate sheet, you write a simple stop condition: if anyone enters the fall area or the setup appears unsafe, stop observing and make the room safe. The sentence seems almost comically unnecessary. You have spent enough of the day with the old records to know that writing an obvious limit can be worth the ink.

requiredPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredPassages.text: Sera arrives with damp knees and a notebook covered in neat arrows. You tell her about the cup. She sets the notebook down and asks three questions: Where was it when the strip appeared? Has anybody moved it since? Is anybody at risk if it breaks? Only after you answer does she ask to inspect the repair.

requiredPassages.speaker: sera
requiredPassages.text: The handle has an old adhesive joint. I can see a dark line. If the cup breaks, that may be ordinary failure under ordinary load. The interesting claim is the timing, not the possibility of a broken cup.

requiredPassages.speaker: ada
requiredPassages.text: We could put it on the floor.

requiredPassages.speaker: sera
requiredPassages.text: We could. Then we would learn what happens when we put it on the floor. We should not confuse intervention with a moral test.

requiredPassages.speaker: tomas
requiredPassages.text: Or with being braver than a piece of paper.

requiredPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredPassages.text: You agree on a modest procedure. Nobody touches the cup for the next few minutes. Nobody stands in the likely fall area. The phone records the table and a clock. If something unsafe happens, you stop the test. A note has made a prediction; it has not earned the right to command anyone's hands.

requiredPassages.speaker: ada
requiredPassages.text: I keep feeling as if moving it would be cheating.

requiredPassages.speaker: sera
requiredPassages.text: That's an important feeling to notice. It is not a rule of physics.

requiredPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredPassages.text: At 16:09, a delivery van rattles past the lane below. The pencils tremble but do not fall. At 16:10, Tomas sneezes and apologizes to the entire room. At 16:11, the kettle clicks off. Each ordinary noise acquires a significance it cannot possibly deserve. You wonder how many omens are created by people waiting beside clocks.

requiredPassages.speaker: ada
requiredPassages.text: What if nothing happens?

requiredPassages.speaker: tomas
requiredPassages.text: We preserve the recording of nothing happening. A sadly underappreciated genre.

requiredPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredPassages.text: The first seconds of 16:12 pass quietly. Then the pressure line beneath the floor knocks once. The table shivers. The repaired handle separates from the cup with a sound no louder than a snapped pencil lead. The cup tips against its own shifted weight, strikes the edge, and falls. Blue pieces scatter inside the empty area you have cleared.

requiredPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredPassages.text: The handle lands beneath the table. It does not roll. On the recording, the clock reads 16:12:08. Nobody speaks until the fragments stop moving.

requiredPassages.speaker: ada
requiredPassages.text: I don't want you to tell me that's impossible.

requiredPassages.speaker: sera
requiredPassages.text: I won't. I want to tell you exactly what we observed.

requiredPassages.speaker: tomas
requiredPassages.text: The cup broke within the stated minute. We took precautions. The line was printed yesterday. We have witnesses and images for both.

requiredPassages.speaker: sera
requiredPassages.text: And we still have ordinary mechanisms for a fragile cup breaking. What we do not yet have is an ordinary explanation for the advance information.

requiredPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredPassages.text: You kneel outside the marked fall area. Beneath the table, just beyond the handle, something catches the light. A brass calibration plate is screwed to the underside of the crossbar. You would never have looked from this angle without following the broken piece.

requiredPassages.speaker: ada
requiredPassages.text: There's a plate here.

requiredPassages.speaker: sera
requiredPassages.text: Don't reach through the shards. I'll bring the torch.

requiredPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredPassages.text: The plate bears the same arcs as the rubbing in Ivo's drawer. Beside them are small letters: TRANSMIT ADVANCE—ONE CYCLE. The lower edge has been obscured by a repair bracket. The handle rests exactly below it, a blue crescent holding your eye in the right place.

requiredPassages.speaker: ada
requiredPassages.text: 'Leave the handle where it falls.' The line wasn't just telling us what happened.

requiredPassages.speaker: tomas
requiredPassages.text: It could be pointing us toward something.

requiredPassages.speaker: sera
requiredPassages.text: That is a plausible interpretation. Let's photograph the plate before we promote it to fact.

requiredPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredPassages.text: Discuss the witnessed prediction without treating it as authority.

conversation.prompt: Discuss the witnessed prediction without treating it as authority.
suggestions: What do we know now that we didn't know this morning?
Can we test the timing without putting anyone at risk?
If this is real, how do we keep it from making decisions for us?
conversation.fallback: We know a documented advance description matched an observed event. Next we investigate a repeatable mechanism with harmless marks and clocks. A forecast still cannot choose what people should value.

requiredPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredPassages.text: Tomas picks up the cup fragments only after you have photographed their positions. He places them in a shallow box with tissue between them. The handle remains where it fell until Sera finishes measuring the plate. Obeying the sentence and documenting a sensible procedure have briefly produced the same behavior. You do not mistake that coincidence for permission to stop judging.

requiredPassages.speaker: ada
requiredPassages.text: I don't want to spend the rest of my life wondering whether every broken thing was arranged to teach me something.

requiredPassages.speaker: tomas
requiredPassages.text: Then don't. Most things break because they're tired.

requiredPassages.speaker: sera
requiredPassages.text: Including institutions. Though they tend to charge more for the repair.

requiredPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredPassages.text: Your laughter arrives late and lasts longer than the joke. When it ends, the fear has not gone. It has acquired edges. You can name the observations. You can name the questions. And this evening, under a tower built before any of you were born, you can examine the machinery that seems to be turning one into the other.

requiredPassages.speaker: narrator
requiredPassages.text: Review the evidence before continuing.
